subject: Globotech: next steps for DPA redlines and transfer assurances
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Gallego <elena.gallego@globotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA redlines and transfer language — initial pass

Elena,

Thanks again for the productive conversation this morning. As discussed, attaching our initial redline of Redwood's standard DPA with a short note callout for international transfer language. Key things we highlighted:

- We kept the core SCC text (EU) but suggested a narrow transfer impact assessment clause rather than prescriptive mitigations.
- Proposed a UK addendum template (see brief in page 3) to address UK IDTA expectations without duplicating obligations.
- Marked two sections where we ask for Globotech to confirm subprocessors used for EU/UK processing and their country locations.

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal teams exchange redlines this week.
2) If both sides can agree on transfer language, we prepare DocuSign envelope for signatures (DPA + Annexes).
3) Globotech to share completed subprocessors table and any SOC/ISO artifacts you can provide.

Attachment: RI_DPA_Sergio_redlines_2026-01-13.pdf (annotated redline)

Happy to hop on a short call if useful — I have availability Thu 10-11am PT.

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Sergio —

Thanks for sending this over. I shared the redline with our legal team and Marco (copied). A few quick items from our side:

- We appreciate the UK addendum template. Our counsel prefers the IDTA approach rather than piecemeal changes in the body of the DPA.
- We have one ask: can Redwood accept a slightly broader transfer impact clause that requires reasonable safeguards & periodic review rather than listing mitigations? Our privacy team will iterate on wording.
- We will assemble the subprocessors table and SOC2 report excerpts; expect those by Monday.

I'll have Marco coordinate the official redline (they prefer to send a track-changes version with comment threads). In the meantime, can your legal (cc Laura if appropriate) confirm whether Redwood needs any additional variance for Switzerland or Norway?

Thanks,
Elena

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Gallego <elena.gallego@globotech.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: DPA redlines and transfer language — draft compromise

Hi Elena, Sergio —

Thanks for the prompt review. I took a pass with the privacy team and drafted a short compromise on the transfer-impact language that should be acceptable to both parties. High level:

- Insert a Transfer Impact Assessment clause that requires the processor (Redwood) to document the legal basis for transfers, adopt appropriate safeguards (SCCs where applicable), and to notify the controller (Globotech) if new subprocessors or transfers to high-risk jurisdictions are planned.
- For Switzerland/Norway: the TIA will include a jurisdiction appendix; Redwood will confirm that SCCs or equivalent safeguards are applied as needed.
- UK IDTA: Rather than a full IDTA, we propose a lightweight UK addendum that mirrors the DPA but references the UK transfer addendum template and allows sign-off via the same DocuSign envelope.

I attached a suggested language snippet and a sample Annex listing subprocessors (placeholder entries) for your counsel to review. If that looks ok I can prepare a clean version for signature and an exportable annex for DocuSign.

Attachment: Globotech_SCCs_proposed_2026-01-15.docx

Proposed quick timeline:
- Mon 19 Jan: receive Globotech redline + subprocessors table
- Tue 20 Jan: finalize language and prepare DocuSign envelope
- Wed 21 Jan: collect signatures

If Globotech prefers a different cadence please let us know.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

We accepted most of the TIA approach but pushed for an explicit monthly notification whenever a new subprocessor is onboarded that will process EU personal data. We also added a sentence requesting that Redwood provide a description of technical and organizational measures (we referenced Annex 2).

I've attached our redline plus a completed subprocessors table (short list) and SOC2 summary excerpts. We are fine with DocuSign execution but would like signatures from both the Redwood corporate entity and the Redwood EMEA subsidiary (for local contracts).

Attachments: Globotech_redline_2026-01-19.docx; Globotech_subprocessors_2026-01-19.csv; Globotech_SOC2_excerpt.pdf
